caption:
Google Play now lets you run Android apps you build with AI, just for yourself.
Build in Google AI Studio, sign in with a normal Google account, and the app stays private to you.
It starts in the U.S. for users 18 and older, with sharing to friends planned next.

What app would you build for yourself?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch · Photos: Google, Kevin Carter / Getty Images

slides.headline: Google Play now lets you vibe code *your own private apps*, no developer account needed

slides.heading: Apps *just for you*
paras: Google announced Tuesday that Android users can run personal apps they create with AI through Google Play, without publishing them to the store.
The apps don't appear in Play search or listings. Only the person who made them can use them.

slides.heading: Built in *AI Studio*
paras: You build the app in Google AI Studio, then launch it on your own phone. A standard Google account is enough, no paid developer account.
It starts in the U.S. for users 18 and older. The apps still have to follow Google Play's policies.

slides.heading: Sharing *comes next*
paras: Google plans to let creators share their apps with a small group of trusted friends in the coming months.

paras.t: Google Play's Sam Bright says the idea is moving from "there's an app for that" to "there's an app for me."

slides.heading: More AI *across Play*
paras: Ask Play, the store's AI assistant, can now compare similar apps. A new AI tool called Game Finder recommends games, first in the U.S.
Play apps and games will also show up more deeply inside Gemini conversations.

slides.hook: Anyone can now build a private Android app with AI. Follow for more tools that turn ideas into apps.
